74076-the-reign-of-king-oberon.title: The Reign Of King Oberon
74076-the-reign-of-king-oberon.creator: Unknown

arxiv-2205-09583.title: Evonne : Interactive Proof Visualization for Description Logics (System Description) — Extended Version
arxiv-2205-09583.creator: Christian Alrabbaa, Franz Baader, Stefan Borgwardt, Raimund Dachselt, Patrick Koopmann, Julián Méndez
arxiv-2205-09583.description: Abstract Explanations for description logic (DL) entailments provide important support for the maintenance of large ontologies. The “justifications” usually employed for this purpose in ontology editors pinpoint the parts of the ontology responsible for a given entailment. Proofs for entailments make the intermediate reasoning steps explicit, and thus explain how a consequence can actually be derived.

arxiv-2501-18555.title: An Empirical Study of Dotfiles Repositories Containing User-Specific Configuration Files
arxiv-2501-18555.creator: Wenhan Zhu, Michael W. Godfrey
arxiv-2501-18555.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wenhan Zhu, Michael W. Godfrey. Storing user-specific configuration files in a “dotfiles” repository is a common practice among software developers, with hundreds of thousands choosing to publicly host their repositories on GitHub . This practice not only provides developers with a simple backup mechanism for their essential configuration files, but also facilitates sharing ideas and learning from others on how best to configure applications that are key to their daily workflows.

arxiv-2505-09760.title: Neural Associative Skill Memories for safer robotics and modelling human sensorimotor repertoires
arxiv-2505-09760.creator: Pranav Mahajan, Mufeng Tang, T. Ed Li, Ioannis Havoutis, Ben Seymour
arxiv-2505-09760.description: Abstract Modern robots face challenges shared by humans, where machines must learn multiple sensorimotor skills and express them adaptively. Equipping robots with a human-like memory of how it feels to do multiple stereotypical movements can make robots more aware of normal operational states and help develop self-preserving safer robots.

arxiv-2506-12150.title: Applications of Combinatorics on Words with Symbolic Dynamics
arxiv-2506-12150.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore applications of combinatorics on words across various domains, including data compression, error detection, cryptographic protocols, and pseudorandom number generation. The examination of the theoretical foundations enabling these applications, emphasizing important concepts of mathematical relationships and algorithms.

arxiv-2512-01399.title: Modeling high-order harmonic generation in quantum dots using a real-space tight-binding approach
arxiv-2512-01399.creator: Martin Thümmler, Alexander Croy, Ulf Peschel, Stefanie Gräfe
arxiv-2512-01399.description: Abstract Recently, the size-dependence of high-order harmonic generation (HHG) in quantum dots has been investigated experimentally. In particular, for longer driving wavelengths and QDs smaller than 3 nm, HHG was strongly suppressed, however, there is no computational model capable of describing the strong-field response of such systems.

arxiv-2602-14937.title: Lattice XBAR Filters in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Thanks: This work was supported by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) under the Compact Front-End Filters at the Element-Level (COFFEE) program No. HR0011-22-2-0031, the National Science Foundation (NSF) under CAREER Award No. 2339

arxiv-2602-14937.description: Abstract This work presents the demonstration of lattice filters based on laterally excited bulk acoustic resonators (XBARs). Two filter implementations, namely direct lattice and layout-balanced lattice topologies, are designed and fabricated in periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN).

pmc-10647597.title: Human Posture Estimation: A Systematic Review on Force-Based Methods—Analyzing the Differences in Required Expertise and Result Benefits for Their Utilization
pmc-10647597.creator: Sebastian Helmstetter, Sven Matthiesen, Li-Fong Lin
pmc-10647597.description: Force-based human posture estimation (FPE) provides a valuable alternative when camera-based human motion capturing is impractical. It offers new opportunities for sensor integration in smart products for patient monitoring, ergonomic optimization and sports science. Due to the interdisciplinary research on the topic, an overview of existing methods and the required expertise for their utilization is lacking.

pmc-10701321.title: Comparison of Capillary Zone Electrophoresis with High-pressure Liquid Chromatography in the Evaluation of Hemoglobinopathies
pmc-10701321.creator: Özlem Çakır Madenci, Özlem Hürmeydan, Asuman Orçun, Fatma Erdoğmuş
pmc-10701321.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:The capillary zone electrophoresis (CZE) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) methods were compared in terms of HbA2 measurement for the assessment of hemoglobinopathies.Materials and Methods:CZE was compared with HPLC for the evaluation of patients without hemoglobinopathy (n=321), with β-thalassemia trait (n=113), and with common (HbD-Punjab, E, C, S/A, and S/S) and rare (HbS/D, O-Arap, Lepore, G-Coushata, Setif, Hamadan, Q-Iran, and H) variants (n=21).

pmc-11433009.title: From a Cup of Tea to Cardiovascular Care: Vascular Mechanisms of Action
pmc-11433009.creator: Marios Sagris, Panayotis K. Vlachakis, Spyridon Simantiris, Panagiotis Theofilis, Maria Gerogianni, Paschalis Karakasis, Konstantinos Tsioufis, Dimitris Tousoulis
pmc-11433009.description: Tea consumption is increasingly recognized for its potential benefits to cardiovascular health. This study reviews the available research, concentrating on the major components of tea and their mechanisms of action in the cardiovascular system. Tea is abundant in bioactive compounds, such as flavonoids and polysaccharides, which possess significant antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

pmc-11605815.title: Development, validation and economic evaluation of a machine learning algorithm for predicting the probability of kidney damage in patients with hyperuricaemia: protocol for a retrospective study
pmc-11605815.creator: Zhengyao Hou, Yong Yang, Bo Deng, Guangjie Gao, Mengting Li, Xinyu Liu, Huan Chang, Hao Shen, Linke Zou, Jinqi Li, Xingwei Wu
pmc-11605815.description: IntroductionAccurate identification of the risk factors is essential for the effective prevention of hyperuricaemia (HUA)-related kidney damage. Previous studies have established the efficacy of machine learning (ML) methodologies in predicting kidney damage due to other chronic diseases. Nevertheless, a scarcity of precise and clinically applicable prediction models exists for assessing the risk of HUA-related kidney damage.

pmc-12384382.title: K-562 Extracellular Vesicles Partially Protect Intact Cells from Oxidative Stress and Provide Limited Resistance to Imatinib
pmc-12384382.creator: Jiana Sbiet, Einat Beery, Zinab Sarsor, Pia Raanani, Orit Uziel
pmc-12384382.description: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) results from the formation of the BCR-ABL1 chimeric protein which serves as a target for clinically used tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as imatinib mesylate (IM). Although very efficient, the development of resistance to TKIs remains a critical issue for a subset of patients.

pmc-12468266.title: The Complete Chloroplast Genomes of Three Manglietia Species and Phylogenetic Insight into the Genus Manglietia Blume
pmc-12468266.creator: Yuan Luo, Wei Luo, Tongxing Zhao, Jing Yang, Lang Yuan, Pinzheng Zhang, Zixin Gong, Haizhu Li, Yongkang Sima, Tao Xu, Madhav Bhatia
pmc-12468266.description: The genus Manglietia Blume is an important group of Magnoliaceae that has high economic and ornamental value. Owing to the small morphological differences among most Manglietia species and the limited sample sizes in previous molecular-level studies, its infrageneric classification remains unclear, and interspecific relationships for some species are still contentious.

pmc-12691273.title: FSH-Induced Nuclear Exclusion of FOXO1 Mediated by PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway in Granulosa Cells Is Associated with Follicle Selection and Growth of the Hen Ovary
pmc-12691273.creator: Chunchi Yan, Yu Ou, Xue Sun, Yuhan Sun, Jinghua Zhao, Ning Qin, Rifu Xu
pmc-12691273.description: Follicle selection is a pivotal process that determines which dominant prehierarchical follicle will enter the preovulatory hierarchy in the hen ovary and directly affects egg-laying productivity, in which granulosa cells (GCs) are characterized by active proliferation and significantly enhanced FSHR mRNA expression.

pmc-13086494.title: Faster fowl fall frequently: speed and force regulation during turning maneuvers by guinea fowl on high and low friction terrains
pmc-13086494.creator: Hannah Goldsmith, Jade Hall, Monica A. Daley
pmc-13086494.description: Safely navigating variable terrains requires animals to balance competing demands of speed, stability, maneuverability and injury avoidance. Straight-line locomotion has been extensively studied, but less is known about how animals coordinate turning maneuvers. The physics of turning creates a coupling between speed, turn sharpness and ground reaction force (GRF) demands, resulting in a trade-off between speed and maneuverability.

pmc-13209167.title: Misalignment Decoupling and Tilt-to-Length Suppression in a Micro-Actuated Beam Steering Mechanism via Nonlinear Cyclic Modulation
pmc-13209167.creator: Yang Li, Changkang Fu, Hongming Zhang, Hongyang Guo, Zhiqiang Zhao, Mengyang Zhao, Ruihong Gao, Qiang Wang, Chen Wang, Caiwen Ma, Dong He, Yongmei Huang
pmc-13209167.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tilt-to-length (TTL) coupling is a critical noise source in high-precision interferometric measurements, particularly in systems involving angular actuation and beam steering. This paper proposes a nonlinear cyclic modulation method to identify lateral misalignment and suppress the associated TTL coupling.

pmc-13287558.title: Sex‐Dependent Neurochemical Encoding of Acute Social Experience in Adult CD1 Mice
pmc-13287558.creator: Garikoitz Azkona, Alina Díez‐Solinska, Oihane Saez‐Atxukarro, Luna Ochoteco‐Perales, Garikoitz Beitia‐Oyarzabal, Oscar Vegas
pmc-13287558.description: Acute social interaction rapidly engages physiological and neurochemical systems, yet the extent to which these responses differ between sexes remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated behavioural, endocrine and region‐specific neurochemical responses to a brief social challenge using the social interaction test in adult male and female CD1 mice.

pmc-13471603.title: Maternal knowledge of neonatal danger signs and associated factors among postpartum mothers attending public health facilities in Adama town, Ethiopia
pmc-13471603.creator: Gemechu Dereje Feyissa, Addis Begashaw, Tilaye Workneh, Ebrahim Mohammed, Tamrat Endebu
pmc-13471603.description: BackgroundThe neonatal period, defined as the first 28 days of life, remains a critical phase for child survival. According to the 2019 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey, the neonatal mortality rate was 33 deaths per 1,000 live births. Despite various interventions, neonatal mortality and morbidities related to neonatal danger signs persist.

pmc-13479805.title: Disulfide engineering of the FANCM–MHF complex reveals constraints on crosslink design in symmetric oligomers
pmc-13479805.creator: Sho Ito, Tatsuya Nishino
pmc-13479805.description: The Fanconi anemia complementation group M protein (FANCM)–MHF complex is required for branched DNA recognition in the Fanconi anemia pathway, but structural analysis of the intact complex has been hindered by dissociation of FANCM from the FANCM‐associated histone fold (MHF) heterotetramer under crystallization conditions.

pmc-13623224.title: Beyond “Middle Power”: Postcolonial Liminality and the Social Construction of Indonesia's Foreign Policy
pmc-13623224.creator: Ahmad Rizky Mardhatillah Umar, Andrew Cooper, David Black, David Hornsby, Emel Parlar Dal
pmc-13623224.description: This article proposes a new framework for understanding Indonesia's foreign policy. I argue that, rather than the widely accepted conception of Indonesia as a middle power, defined in terms of size, capability, identity, or status, Indonesia's foreign policy is better characterized by postcolonial liminality: a position in which Indonesia sits between multiple powers.

pmc-13681264.title: The hidden risk: inadvertent pregnancies in random start ovarian stimulation protocols and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
pmc-13681264.creator: Ayse Seyhan, Bulent Urman, Baris Ata
pmc-13681264.description: ObjectiveTo examine the risk of severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) when random-start ovarian stimulation (RSOS) is performed during an undetected, spontaneously conceived pregnancy.DesignA case-reportSubjectsA 24-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome, a history of two early pregnancy losses, and 25 months of infertility, who underwent in vitro fertilization (IVF) with RSOS at an external fertility clinic.
